messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: apac-prim-1 GPU pool saturating — queue length 12.3k, avg latency 1.9s, recent autoscale attempts failing (3/3) with ProvisioningTimeout. Pager: @emma oncall.

emma: picking this up — I'm on the call loop. initial triage: autoscaler attempted 2x scale-ups but new nodes remained in Pending for >5m. logs show API quota errors from k8s provider.

raj: I see the provider quota error too: `Allocation failed: quotaExceeded` in the cluster events. Looks like we hit a regional GPU quota. apac account shows no remaining GPU quota to spin new nodes.

emma: confirmed. autoscaler is stuck in cooldown because controllers keep trying and failing. queue is building. Can we temporarily spillover to eu1?

mike: cross-region spillover already configured, but last test showed some model-variant mismatches for the hot model (quantized-v2) in eu1; fallback auto-switching is enabled but the variant registry doesn't have a compatible shard for a subset of requests, so around 30% of requests are failing validation and getting retried, amplifying queue.

sophie: any customer impact yet? support says a handful of customers reported slow responses and increased 503s for long-form generation. Not widespread yet but growing.

carlos: onboarded enterprise customers with Reserved pools unaffected, but shared-hosted customers on apac are hit. we should prepare a status page blurb.

emma: plan proposal: 1) pause autoscaler attempts (to stop churn), 2) temporarily disable cross-region spillover for apac-prim-1 to avoid cascading failures into eu1, 3) manually route high-priority reserved traffic to eu1 warm standby (explicit route), 4) apply rate-limit to non-SLA hostnames. Thoughts?

raj: +1 for pause autoscaler. We can set an annotation to disable scaling: `kubectl annotate hpa/autoscaler disabled=true --overwrite`. I'll do that. Also can we request emergency quota from cloud provider? That takes time.

emma: do the annotation. mike — can you flip spillover off for that pool? simple config toggle in routing service: `route-config set apac-prim-1.spillover=false`.

mike: doing it now. flipping in 1m, pushing a canary, then global roll apply.

deploy-bot: deploy started by mike: apply route-config apac-prim-1.spillover=false -> canary -> 5/5 success -> promoting.

mike: spillover disabled. confirming eu1 error rate is dropping from side-effect retries. but now apac queue will stay local and must be drained.

emma: raj, please annotate HPA to stop additional scale attempts. also add a manual annotation so autoscaler does not resume until we clear.

raj: done: `kubectl annotate hpa/autoscaler disabled=true --overwrite` and added runbook tag: `recovery:apac-cooldown-stall-2419003333`.

emma: support/carlos — please craft a status page entry: short impact: "Increased latency and errors for shared-hosted customers in APAC due to GPU provisioning failures; mitigation ongoing." mark severity: degraded.

carlos: status drafted and published. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2419003333-apac-gpu-provisioning. includes customer guidance to retry or failover to eu region.

sophie: ops question: if we disable spillover we avoid cascading, but what about legacy traffic that expects eu fallback? can we route only premium traffic to eu1 while keeping spillover off for best-effort?

mike: yes — we can set selective routing by tag. I'll create a temporary intent: route TAG:premium->eu1, TAG:best-effort->local. Pushing policy now.

deploy-bot: policy update applied: premium->eu1 (priority) ; best-effort->apac-local.

emma: good. queue is still high but not increasing as fast. next actions: evict some cached KV shards to free memory, restart a few long-running workers to reclaim stuck GPU slots, and attempt a controlled rolling restart of the scheduling agent. raj, can you coordinate with infra?

raj: starting worker restarts in staggered batches (2 at a time) to avoid mass eviction. also clearing stale KV cache entries from model-cache with TTL flush: `curl -X POST https://cache.internal/flush -d '{"pattern":"apac-prim-1/*"}'`. Doing it now.

mike: I restarted 2 workers. reclaiming ~2 GPUs worth of free slots. queue dropped by ~800 after first batch.

emma: nice. support notes: customers affected: list from support tool: shared-acct-423, shared-acct-998, shared-quickstart. please tag for follow-up and credits.

carlos: tagged them in support tracker and queued refunds/credits per policy.

raj: cloud provider responded to emergency request — they can free up 4 GPUs in ~18m if we accept a quota reallocation. That will allow autoscaler to succeed.

emma: ok plan B: keep autoscaler paused, continue manual drain and restarts, accept quota reallocation, and once new nodes are provisioned flip autoscaler back on with a warm-start flag to avoid immediate churn. mike — can you prepare the warm-start config?

mike: yes. warm-start toggles kernel prewarm and immediately registers nodes as available but schedules with low concurrency. I'll prepare staging and a safe rollout: `scale-policy warm-start=true initial-concurrency=1`.

deploy-bot: cloud quota update accepted: +4 GPUs allocated to apac account (ticket #CLOUD-7890).

raj: new nodes are provisioning — k8s events show nodes ready in ~9m and autoscaler still paused.

emma: once nodes report Ready, we'll validate: run a small traffic shadow test to eu1 and local to ensure model compatibility. If clear, flip autoscaler back on with warm-start.

mike: traffic shadow test passed 95% for quantized-v2; failures were for a narrow subset of request headers that had a different model param — we've mapped those and will add a variant mapping so eu1 can accept them.

emma: good. I will re-enable autoscaler after warm-start config applied. also creating a follow-up action item: automate quota-fallback notifications so oncall can see provider limits earlier.

emma: re-enabling autoscaler now with warm-start.

deploy-bot: apply hpa/autoscaler annotations removed: disabled=false; apply scale-policy warm-start=true.

emma: autoscaler back online. watching queue metrics.

mike: queue dropping steadily, latency normalizing, error rate down. will keep selective spillover off for 1hr to avoid surprises.

sophie: product note: creating post-incident eval to assess quality regressions and customer-facing impact. will coordinate with ML infra on variant mappings and automated fallback tests.

carlos: status page updated: Mitigation in progress, partial restoration observed. We'll move to resolved once metrics are stable for 30m.

emma: closing notes: root cause: regional GPU quota exhausted + autoscaler retry cooldown loop causing provisioning churn; secondary contributor: permissive spillover that amplified retries to eu1 because of model-variant incompatibility.

action items (short):
- infra: automate provider quota alerting (raj)
- routing: add selective spillover by customer-tag (mike)
- ml infra: variant registry compatibility checks on spillover (raj + sophie)
- support: customer credits & comms (carlos)

emma: handing off to follow-up owners. On-call cleared for now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
